features.label: Connection transport (ICE / DTLS)

patches.author: stransky
patches.subject: Make nr_crypto_nss_hmac() work with FIPS enabled

patches.author: Sylvestre Ledru
patches.subject: Declare every about:license notice in moz.build

features.summary: Firefox’s WebRTC connection security can now use HMAC, a method for checking message integrity, when FIPS cryptography rules are enabled—helping secure connections work in regulated environments. The other change updates how license notices are tracked during builds; it does not alter browser behavior.

features.label: WebRTC

patches.author: Martin Sirringhaus
patches.subject: Make WebRTC work with FIPS enabled

patches.author: Jan-Niklas Jaeschke
patches.subject: Part 2: Qualify mozilla::Range<T> ahead of nsRange rename.

features.summary: Firefox’s WebRTC features can now work when FIPS cryptography rules are enabled, supporting secure connections in regulated environments. A separate internal adjustment prepares WebRTC code for a rename of a browser range-selection type, with no user-visible change.

features.label: Negotiation engine (JSEP)

patches.author: Anna Weine
patches.subject: Reject local descriptions whose DTLS fingerprint was modified

features.summary: WebRTC now rejects a local connection description if its DTLS fingerprint—the value used to verify the other side’s secure connection—has been changed. This helps prevent a modified description from undermining the connection’s identity check.

features.label: Video Engine

patches.author: Jan-Ivar Bruaroey
patches.subject: Store desktop capture sources in an nsTArray instead of a map.

features.summary: The video engine’s internal storage for desktop capture sources was changed. This is an implementation detail, with no user-visible behavior change indicated by the patch title.

features.label: WebRTC web API (RTCPeerConnection)

patches.author: serge-sans-paille
patches.subject: Replace std::string::find(...) == 0 by std::string::starts_with

features.summary: This was a small internal cleanup to the RTCPeerConnection WebRTC API, which websites use to set up real-time audio and video connections. It changes how Firefox checks whether text begins with a given prefix, without changing the API’s behavior for users or websites.

features.summary: WebRTC’s ICE network connections and DTLS secure transports were made more robust, including support for restarting DTLS and fixes for stalled ICE checks and stream removal. Changes to remote-candidate handling and media-packet notification order also help connection events be processed consistently; several accompanying updates are internal maintenance to the mDNS service and transport code.

patches.subject: Make RTCSessionDescription.type/sdp readonly.

patches.subject: Add an interop mochitest for Video Orientation signaling and receive.

patches.subject: Support Video Orientation RTP header extension: signaling and receive path.

patches.subject: Add a MID-only demux test for early media reoffers.

patches.author: Daniel Baker
patches.subject: Add early media reoffer test coverage.

patches.author: Paul Adenot
patches.subject: Handle rejection of fire-and-forget play() calls in WebRTC mochitest helpers.

features.summary: WebRTC gained support for signaling and receiving video orientation through an RTP header extension, along with receiving video’s dependency-descriptor extension. New tests cover these features and early-media renegotiation, where media can arrive before setup is complete; related updates also improve getUserMedia source telemetry and align session-description fields with the API’s read-only rules.

features.summary: Firefox corrected how its Session Description Protocol (SDP)—the format WebRTC uses to agree on connection and media settings—reads AV1 profile and level details. This helps peers negotiate AV1 video correctly. Related changes reorganize SDP’s shared building blocks, making the code easier to maintain; these are not visible to users.

patches.subject: Support early media reception for bundled recvonly/sendrecv transceivers.

features.summary: The WebRTC call API now supports provisional answers and early media reception for bundled connections, so audio or video can arrive before negotiation is fully complete. Codec preferences are carried through to sending, AV1 codec matching is more accurate, and InsertDTMF—the API for sending telephone keypad tones—better follows its specification. Additional fixes address frame handling and ICE timing or error cases.

patches.author: Anna Weine
patches.subject: Update webrtcdtls.KEA to FF 164

features.summary: WebRTC, the technology behind browser video calls, now works with FIPS-enabled security settings and better respects the negotiated H.264 and AV1 video limits, so calls can use compatible video sizes and frame rates. Firefox also reports capture-size changes only when they really happen and updates its DTLS security settings; other patches mainly improve codec capability checks and code quality.

patches.subject: Serialize MediaCapabilities encode-support probes through an encoder AllocPolicy.

patches.subject: Add PEMFactory::StrictSupportsAsync and strict WebRTC encode support path for MediaCapabilities.

patches.subject: Add strict create-and-probe WebRTC decode support path for MediaCapabilities.

patches.subject: Replace duplicate WebRTC codec-support pref-gating closures with shared functions.

patches.subject: Route MediaCapabilities WebRTC and encode paths through async codec support.

patches.author: Andreas Pehrson
patches.subject: Handle AV1 when checking for platform decoder.

features.summary: Firefox now checks WebRTC audio and video codec support through more consistent, asynchronous probes, including stricter checks for whether encoding and decoding will work and whether AV1 has a platform decoder. It also gives libwebrtc better information for adjusting video quality and keeps track of who is sending audio or video, helping calls adapt and report media sources reliably.

patches.author: Daniel Baker
patches.subject: Enhance CanTentativelyReceive() to cover reoffers of already-negotiated transceivers.

features.summary: Firefox’s WebRTC negotiation now rejects connection descriptions if their DTLS fingerprint—the identity check used to secure the connection—has been changed. It also negotiates AV1 settings and RTP header extensions more accurately, improving compatibility when calls start or renegotiate media.

features.label: Camera & audio capture

patches.author: Andreas Pehrson
patches.subject: Apply capture rotation centrally, behind a pref.

patches.author: Andreas Pehrson
patches.subject: Don't swap the requested frame dimensions for rotated frames.

patches.author: Daniel Baker
patches.subject: Add a fake-camera test pattern for pixel-level rotation tests.

patches.author: Daniel Baker
patches.subject: Add media.getusermedia.camera.fake.rotation pref for testing.

features.summary: Camera rotation is now applied in one central place, while keeping the requested video dimensions unchanged. A built-in test pattern and testing preference help verify that rotated camera video appears correctly; these changes are mainly about consistent capture behavior and testing, with no intended visible change for most users.

features.label: libwebrtc build

patches.author: Dan Baker
patches.subject: updated default_config_env for v155

patches.author: Dan Baker
patches.subject: updated default_config_env for v154

features.summary: The default build configuration was updated for libwebrtc versions 154 and 155. This keeps Firefox’s build settings aligned with the versions of the WebRTC calling engine it integrates.

features.label: Android camera capture

patches.author: Andreas Pehrson
patches.subject: Report rotation from the Android capture backend instead of applying it.

features.summary: On Android, the camera capture backend now reports the camera’s rotation directly instead of Firefox rotating the frames afterward. This keeps orientation information tied to the platform source and avoids duplicate or inconsistent rotation handling.

features.label: Libwebrtc Overrides

patches.author: Jens Stutte
patches.subject: Use std::source_location in WebrtcLocation.

features.summary: WebRTC’s diagnostic location information now uses C++ std::source_location, allowing source file and line details to be captured by the language rather than maintained through custom arguments. This is an internal reliability and maintainability improvement with no expected user-facing change.

features.label: Transportbridge

patches.author: Andreas Pehrson
patches.subject: Handle MediaTrackGraph promises on AbstractThread::MainThread().

features.summary: Media-track operations now handle their completion signals on the browser’s main thread, where they can be coordinated safely with other browser activity. This is an internal reliability change, with no intended visible change for users.

features.label: Video Engine

patches.author: Jan-Ivar Bruaroey
patches.subject: Store desktop capture sources in an nsTArray instead of a map.

features.summary: The video engine’s internal storage for desktop capture sources was changed. This is an implementation detail, with no user-visible behavior change indicated by the patch title.
